title: How to Calculate the Break-Even Point of a Business in Nepal
metaDescription: Learn how to calculate your business break-even point in Nepalese Rupees. Separate fixed from variable costs and determine required sales volume.
h1: How to Calculate the Break-Even Point of a Business
directAnswer: To calculate the break-even point of a business in Nepal, divide total fixed operating costs (rent, base salaries, insurance, depreciation) by the contribution margin ratio (Sales Price per unit minus Variable Cost per unit, divided by Sales Price). The resulting NPR figure represents the exact sales revenue needed to cover all expenses with zero net profit and zero net loss.
author: Lalitpur Advisory Research Desk

sections.contentHtml:
A break-even analysis establishes your commercial baseline: how much revenue must your team generate each month before making a single rupee of profit?

Break-Even Revenue (NPR) = Fixed Costs / Contribution Margin Ratio
Where: Contribution Margin Ratio = (Selling Price - Variable Cost) / Selling Price

Fixed Operating Costs (Monthly)

  • Office / Retail Store Rent in Lalitpur or Kathmandu
  • Administrative & Core Staff Payroll
  • Software Subscriptions & Accounting Fees
  • Bank Loan Interest & Depreciation

Variable Costs (Per Unit Sold)

  • Product Wholesale / Manufacturing Cost
  • Packaging Materials & Delivery Courier Fees
  • Sales Commissions & POS Card Merchant Fees
  • Direct Production Utilities

sections.h2: Sample Nepal Case Study: Lalitpur Retail Coffee Shop
sections.contentHtml: Consider a retail coffee shop in Kumaripati with monthly fixed overhead of NPR 180,000 (rent, baristas, electricity). Each coffee sells for NPR 300, with variable bean, milk, and packaging costs of NPR 120 (Contribution margin = NPR 180 per cup). To break even, the shop must sell: NPR 180,000 / 180 = 1,000 cups per month (or ~33 cups per day). Every cup sold beyond 33 yields pure pre-tax operating profit. Learn more via our corporate profitability analysis.

faqs.question: How often should a business recalculate its break-even point?
faqs.answer: Recalculate whenever major cost inputs shift: e.g., following minimum wage adjustments under Nepal Labor Act notifications or commercial rental increases.
